requirement: Implement TimezoneCalculator supporting aware UTC normalization, elapsed hours between datetimes, ambiguous DST fold resolution, and wall-clock preserving calendar math.
skeleton: TimezoneCalculator class with datetime and zoneinfo timezone operations.

rationale.teaches: Aware-datetime arithmetic: astimezone for conversion, a naive-input guard, fold to resolve ambiguous DST times, and calendar-day math that preserves wall-clock time across a transition.
rationale.why: replace versus astimezone and UTC-based versus calendar-based day math both give the right answer most of the year and the wrong one across a DST boundary. The fixture uses transition dates, where the difference is one hour.

candidates.why_wrong: replace(tzinfo=utc) relabels the time instead of converting it, so a 10:00 New York time becomes 10:00 UTC.
Naive datetimes are accepted, so elapsed hours between a naive and an aware value raises TypeError from the subtraction.
fold is always 0, so an ambiguous time during the DST fallback always resolves to the first occurrence.
Adding days in UTC and converting back shifts the wall-clock hour across a DST transition.
Elapsed hours is computed from the hour fields alone, so any span crossing midnight or spanning days is wrong.
